resources.string: No firmware yet: connect to the internet and tap "Check GitHub for newer firmware".
This phone has no USB host (OTG) support.
No board on USB. Connect the board with a USB-OTG adapter and a data cable (a charge-only cable shows nothing).
Firmware and web client. The board gets a new identity and device password; its settings start over. Use this the first time.
Keeps identity, settings and stored messages.
The board gets a new identity and device password, and its Wi-Fi and LoRa settings start over.
Done. The board restarts with the new firmware. Open the board log to see its hotspot name and device password.
Restarts the board and shows what it prints: hotspot name, device password, BLE passkey, what it hears.
Sets the network the board joins, over this USB cable (the board\'s own USB socket). No hotspot or switch needed. Needs the firmware from 0.1.1-beta9 on.
Saved. With the setup switch off, the board joins %1$s now.
The hotspot is opening: join Mava-XXXX with the device password (Board log shows both).
Hotspot back to normal: on only with the setup switch on or no Wi-Fi saved.
The board\'s firmware is older: install the new firmware first (Update firmware only).

• Hold BOOT, press and release RESET, release BOOT, then try again.
• On a dev board with two USB sockets, use the one marked USB.
• The Mava firmware needs an ESP32-S3 with 16 MB flash and 8 MB PSRAM (N16R8).
• The keyboard module (Raspberry Pi Pico) is flashed from a computer, with the Linux flasher.
Downloaded firmware %1$s (signature and SHA-256 checked). Flash it with the buttons below.
Could not check GitHub: %1$s. The firmware shown is used.

Without a LoRa module (SX1262) fitted, tell the board so: it then skips the radio at boot (looking for a missing module holds Bluetooth up for 10–20 s) and sends nothing to the air. Over this USB cable; firmware 0.1.1-beta29 on. Also on the board\'s screen: Settings.
Saved: the board skips the radio from now on.
Saved: the board looks for the LoRa module now (the board log shows if it was found).
On: the Screen tab can be the board\'s screen, keys, speaker and microphone over USB.
Off: the firmware without them, faster. For a board with its own display and keys; the Screen tab does nothing.
No board on USB. Connect it with a USB-OTG adapter and a data cable, to the board\'s own USB socket.
This board has no screen UI, or its firmware is older than 0.1.1-beta11: update it in the Flash tab.
The board refused to share its screen.
The board does not answer: is the Mava firmware running? (Flash tab → Board log)
Type with the phone\'s keyboard (hide the board\'s touch keyboard)

Touch the picture to tap the handheld\'s screen. The buttons are its keys: call, menu, arrows, OK, back, end. Text you type here goes to the board as key presses, in any language your phone\'s keyboard has. The Flash tab and this one take turns with the board\'s USB; close Mava\'s LoRa-over-USB first.
Show the board\'s screen here (off: keys and keyboard only, the board\'s own display shows it)
Board sound on this phone\'s speaker
This phone\'s microphone to the board
The board does not take audio: update it to firmware 0.1.1-beta32 or later (pre-release builds only).
The Screen tab is a pre-release tool: the phone stands in for the handheld\'s screen, keys, speaker and microphone while the hardware is being built. Version 1 boards do without it.
